chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not leave (saying) 'In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful', even if a poem follows it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on reciting Basmala before poetry in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) extends the sanctity of the Basmala beyond ritual acts to include the recitation of poetry, reflecting the Shia emphasis on infusing all aspects of life with divine remembrance. This instruction underscores the virtue of maintaining spiritual awareness even in secular or literary contexts, ensuring that artistic expression is accompanied by the invocation of Allah’s mercy. The ruling highlights the continuity of sacred language in daily life, bridging the gap between ritual piety and cultural practice.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Amro Bin Abdul Aziz, from Jameel Bin Darraj who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not leave (the saying of) ‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Beneficent, the Merciful’, and even though after it is a poem’.
en.sarwar: 1. Allah Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz from Jamil ibn Darraj who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Do not ignore the expression, “(I begin) in the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful,” even if it is followed by a poem.’”
